extracted.intended_audience: computational_narrative researchers, story-generation practitioners, and writers interested in narrative evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluation methods for assessing AI-generated (and human-authored) narratives, emphasizing causal coherence, character intentionality, affect, plausibility, and formal metrics used in computational creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The perception by the audience that the main events follow logically from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each event must be motivated by what came before; nothing should appear arbitrary. Evaluate whether there is a coherent causal chain among events rather than a mere sequence of happenings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Believability
rubrics_metrics.description: The perception by the audience that the actions performed by characters do not negatively impact the audience's suspension of disbelief; characters must be perceived as intentional agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters must have goals; their actions must serve those goals; their goals must be intelligible given who they are. Believability is judged by whether readers can see characters as goal-directed agents rather than arbitrary plot devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent-Based Action Explanation (IPOCL requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every character action must be explainable by an attributable intention (goal) that the character is pursuing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond causal plot links, each action should admit a plausible intention — a story fails when a character does something for which we cannot construct an intent. This is a craft criterion used by Riedl's planner (IPOCL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affective Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should invoke emotional responses in readers (e.g., suspense, surprise, sympathy, fear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether the text actually produces emotional effects; note that surface linguistic features have low correlation with emotional effect and affect is hard to predict from text alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commonsense Plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must satisfy implicit social norms — characters behave in socially intelligible ways unless deviation is explicitly the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether character behaviors and social interactions conform to background commonsense expectations; flag deviations only when deliberately motivated by plot or characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatiotemporal Continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative must preserve spatial and temporal continuity (e.g., characters cannot be in two places at once; time should not run backward without notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for continuity errors in locations, character positions, and timeline sequencing; such errors break the story world and harm immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated stories should exhibit recognizable dramatic shape — rising action, climax, resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative shows a dramatic arc rather than reading as a mere chronicle of events. Dramatic shape contributes to perceived story-ness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / Tellability
rubrics_metrics.description: A story should be worth telling — contain something unexpected, surprising, or non-trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story contains non-routine, interesting events or insights; routine sequences that add no newsworthiness or narrative value are not considered tellable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Ratings on Narrative Dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use human judges to rate stories on dimensions such as coherence, believability, affect, structure, and tellability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit human judgments for the perceptual dimensions listed above; human ratings are a primary evaluation method in computational creativity for capturing subjective responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional Reasoning Trace
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether plausible character intentions can be recovered for each action in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to reconstruct an intention/explanation trace for actions; the ease and plausibility of recovering intentions is used as an evaluative signal for character believability and IPOCL compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot-Graph Distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how far the generated structure deviates from canonical plot templates using graph-based representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute structural distance between the generated plot graph and known or canonical templates to quantify novelty vs. conformity and detect structural incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise vs. Suspense Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative metrics (e.g., information-theoretic measures) that distinguish surprise from suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calibrated information-theory based measures to assess unexpectedness (surprise) and buildable tension (suspense); these complement human affect ratings and structural metrics.
